title: Profitability financing and efficiency
goal: Use margin, ROA, debt-to-equity, and asset turnover to support a qualified business conclusion.

slides.title: How well does the business use its resources?
slides.takeaway: Use the same two-year case for all four ratios.
slides.notes: These are full years, separate from Summit Trail’s startup month. Prior ending assets equal the next year’s beginning assets.

slides.title: Calculate net profit margin
slides.takeaway: Net income is $0.125 per $1 of revenue.
slides.notes: Year 1: $9,000 / $90,000 = 10%. Net profit margin is different from gross margin.

slides.title: Use average assets to calculate ROA
slides.takeaway: Match period profit with the resources used during that period.
slides.notes: Use the simple beginning/end average here. More frequent averages can help when assets change substantially during a year. Never assume missing beginning assets are zero.

slides.title: Define the debt-to-equity convention
slides.takeaway: This course uses all liabilities in the numerator.
slides.notes: Some references use only interest-bearing debt. Confirm the definition before comparing. Both balances are from the same date; Year 1 is also 1.50.

slides.title: Calculate asset turnover with average assets
slides.notes: Year 1: $90,000 / $75,000 = 1.20. More assets do not automatically improve revenue generated per asset dollar.

slides.title: Use periods, units, and comparisons consistently
slides.takeaway: Monthly ratios are not directly comparable to full-year ratios.
slides.notes: If beginning balances are missing, say average-based ratios cannot be calculated reliably. Label any permitted alternative explicitly. Match policies and business models too.

slides.title: Handle zero denominators and negative equity

items.heading: Zero denominator
items.text: Report the ratio as undefined or not meaningful and explain why.

items.heading: Negative equity
items.text: Negative debt-to-equity does not mean low financial risk.

slides.takeaway: A spreadsheet result still needs interpretation.
slides.notes: Negative profit with positive revenue can produce meaningful loss margins and ROA. Do not generalize the negative-equity caution to every negative ratio. Near-zero denominators also produce unstable results.

slides.title: Try it: compare two periods and explain the drivers
slides.takeaway: Higher margin more than offset lower turnover in ROA.
slides.notes: Using unrounded values, margin × turnover = ROA under these definitions. Do not claim a cause without evidence about prices, costs, or asset use.

items: Profitability improved: margin and ROA rose.
Turnover fell: revenue grew more slowly than average assets.
The liabilities-to-equity proportion stayed the same.

slides.title: Support one recommendation with the numbers

items.heading: Evidence
items.text: Margin rose to 12.5%; turnover fell to 1.11 times.

items.heading: Interpretation
items.text: Profitability improved while revenue per asset dollar weakened.

items.heading: Recommendation
items.text: Review utilization of recent asset additions.

slides.takeaway: Request capacity and sales evidence before deciding to invest more.
slides.notes: A qualified fictional teaching recommendation. Distinguish a plausible explanation from an established cause.
